accepted.s: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 is called the “Mini-Constitution” primarily because it:
o: replaced the parliamentary form of government with a presidential form
introduced the system of judicial review in India
abolished the office of the President
made sweeping changes in several parts of the Constitution
accepted.x: The 42nd Amendment is known as the “Mini-Constitution” because of its wide-ranging and sweeping changes to the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that explains the famous title rather than merely naming an associated provision.
accepted.sec: 42nd Amendment - words added to the Preamble, year, "Mini-Constitution"  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:
1. It was enacted during the Emergency of 1975–77.
2. It was enacted under the leadership of Indira Gandhi.
3. It was the Second Amendment of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the relevant amendment was the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, not the Second Amendment.
accepted.tq: Split the options by identifying the wrong amendment number in the confusable statement.
accepted.sec: 42nd Amendment - words added to the Preamble, year, "Mini-Constitution"  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
o: Abolition of the power of judicial review in its entirety
Freezing of delimitation of parliamentary seats
Introduction of Fundamental Duties
Addition of new Directive Principles of State Policy
accepted.x: The 42nd Amendment curtailed judicial review and attempted to exclude it in certain matters, but it did not abolish the power of judicial review in its entirety.
accepted.tq: Find the extreme statement that goes beyond the stated effect of the amendment.
accepted.sec: 42nd Amendment - words added to the Preamble, year, "Mini-Constitution"  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which case struck down the provisions of the 42nd Constitutional Amendment that sought to give Parliament unlimited amending power and exclude judicial review?
o: LIC of India case
Minerva Mills case
Berubari Union case
Kesavananda Bharati case
accepted.x: In Minerva Mills (1980), the Supreme Court struck down the clauses of the 42nd Amendment that attempted to confer unlimited amending power on Parliament and exclude judicial review.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional consequence with the correct Supreme Court case.
accepted.sec: 42nd Amendment - words added to the Preamble, year, "Mini-Constitution"  [APPSC]

b. New Directive Principles of State Policy

accepted.s: In the Berubari Union case, the Supreme Court held that the Preamble:
o: was an integral part of the Constitution and could be amended under Article 368
formed the basic structure and could not be referred to for interpretation
was not a part of the Constitution, but could guide interpretation where an Article was ambiguous
was enforceable by constitutional courts as a source of legislative power
accepted.x: In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Preamble was held not to be a part of the Constitution, although it was regarded as a key to the minds of the framers and an aid to interpretation in cases of ambiguity.
accepted.tq: Separate the case’s holding on constitutional status from its limited interpretative use.
accepted.sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of the Kesavananda Bharati judgment on the Preamble?
o: It held that the Preamble was enforceable independently of the Fundamental Rights.
It reaffirmed that the Preamble was not part of the Constitution.
It held that the Preamble was part of the Constitution and could be amended, subject to the basic structure limitation.
It held that the Preamble was part of the Constitution and could not be amended in any circumstance.
accepted.x: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) overruled the Berubari position by recognizing the Preamble as part of the Constitution. It may be amended under Article 368, but its basic structure cannot be destroyed.
accepted.tq: Distinguish amendability from the limitation imposed by the basic structure doctrine.
accepted.sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Berubari Union — 1960
2. Kesavananda Bharati — 1973
3. LIC of India — 1995

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Berubari Union was decided in 1960, Kesavananda Bharati in 1973 and LIC of India in 1995. All three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Use the year as the anchor and verify each case-year pair independently.
accepted.sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court in LIC of India (1995) described the Preamble as:
o: an enforceable code of administrative conduct
a source of independent legislative power
a non-constitutional political resolution
an integral part of the Constitution
accepted.x: The LIC of India judgment (1995) recognized the Preamble as an integral part of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Identify the later judicial position rather than the earlier Berubari view.
accepted.sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the enactment of the Preamble is correct?
o: It was added by the Constituent Assembly after the commencement of the Constitution.
It was enacted before the remaining provisions of the Constitution.
It was enacted after the rest of the Constitution had already been enacted, so that it would fit the constitutional text.
It was enacted simultaneously with the Objectives Resolution in 1946.
accepted.x: The Preamble was enacted after the rest of the Constitution had been enacted, enabling it to conform to the constitutional text.
accepted.tq: Test the sequence of enactment rather than the date of commencement.
accepted.sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A court is interpreting an ambiguous constitutional provision. Which role may the Preamble properly perform in such a situation?
o: It may independently create a new legislative power.
It may serve as an aid to interpretation.
It may invalidate every law inconsistent with any Preamble ideal.
It may be enforced as a separate fundamental right.
accepted.x: The Preamble may guide courts in interpreting ambiguous constitutional provisions. It is neither an independent source of legislative power nor an enforceable set of rights.
accepted.tq: Apply the interpretative role of the Preamble to an ambiguity-based scenario.
accepted.sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the legal effect of the Preamble:
1. It is not a source of power for the legislature.
2. It is not a limitation on powers expressly granted by the Constitution.
3. It is non-justiciable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Preamble does not confer legislative power, does not limit powers expressly granted by the Constitution, and cannot be directly enforced by a court.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the distinct legal effects of the Preamble.
accepted.sec: Is the Preamble part of the Constitution - Berubari, Kesavananda, LIC; enactment, legal effect, enforceability  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of the forms of Justice mentioned in the Preamble?
o: Economic, political and social
Political, social and economic
Social, political and economic
Social, economic and political
accepted.x: The Preamble promises Justice—social, economic and political—in that order.
accepted.tq: Read the constitutional expression in its exact order rather than recalling only the three words.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the forms of Liberty mentioned in the Preamble?
o: Expression, thought, faith, belief and worship
Thought, expression, faith, belief and worship
Thought, belief, expression, faith and worship
Thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
accepted.x: The Preamble refers to Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.
accepted.tq: Use exact-word and exact-order discrimination for a constitutional phrase.
accepted.sec: Preamble text - words present vs absent, order, original wording  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Preamble promises equality of:
o: status and opportunity
law and administration
income and wealth
rights and duties
accepted.x: The Preamble assures equality of status and of opportunity. It does not use the expression “equality of rights” in this formulation.
accepted.tq: Reject the familiar-looking phrase and identify the exact constitutional wording.
accepted.sec: Preamble text - words present vs absent, order, original wording  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly completes the Preamble’s description of Fraternity?
o: Assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation
Assuring social justice and economic democracy
Assuring equality of law and liberty of action
Assuring the sovereignty and territorial integrity of India
accepted.x: Fraternity in the Preamble assures the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation.
accepted.tq: Complete the precise constitutional phrase instead of substituting a related ideal.
accepted.sec: Preamble text - words present vs absent, order, original wording  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the original wording of the Preamble as adopted in 1949?
o: Sovereign Secular Democratic Republic and unity of the Nation
Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic and unity and integrity of the Nation
Sovereign Democratic Republic and unity of the Nation
Sovereign Democratic Socialist Republic and integrity of the Nation
accepted.x: The original 1949 Preamble described India as a “Sovereign Democratic Republic” and referred to the “unity of the Nation.”
accepted.tq: Compare the original text with the words introduced later by constitutional amendment.
accepted.sec: Preamble text - words present vs absent, order, original wording  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following terms does NOT occur in the Preamble to the Constitution of India?
o: Fraternity
Democratic
Federal
Republic
accepted.x: The term “Federal” or “Federation” does not occur in the Preamble. “Democratic,” “Republic” and “Fraternity” are present.
accepted.tq: Find the absent constitutional term among closely related Preamble expressions.
accepted.sec: Preamble text - words present vs absent, order, original wording  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs consists entirely of expressions absent from the Preamble?
o: Equality and Fraternity
Federal and Fundamental Duties
Democratic and Republic
Justice and Liberty
accepted.x: “Federal” and “Fundamental Duties” are absent from the Preamble. Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, Democratic and Republic are present.
accepted.tq: Use elimination by recognizing the core ideals explicitly named in the Preamble.
accepted.sec: Preamble text - words present vs absent, order, original wording  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following expressions is NOT found in the Preamble?
o: Unity and integrity of the Nation
Dignity of the individual
Adult franchise
Economic justice
accepted.x: The Preamble does not contain the expression “adult franchise.” It does refer to unity and integrity of the Nation, dignity of the individual and economic justice.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a constitutional principle mentioned elsewhere from the exact contents of the Preamble.
accepted.sec: Preamble text - words present vs absent, order, original wording  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the wording of the Preamble is correct?
o: It assures liberty of movement, residence, occupation and worship.
It assures equality of income, status and political representation.
It assures liberty of action and equality of rights.
It assures liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship, and equality of status and opportunity.
accepted.x: The Preamble specifically mentions liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship, and equality of status and opportunity. “Liberty of action” and “equality of rights” are not its expressions.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between exact Preamble wording and plausible but absent substitutes.
accepted.sec: Preamble text - words present vs absent, order, original wording  [APPSC]
